I'm going to write the answer now, without putting any code inside a sentence. I'll include the doc path, src/docs/architecture/06-runtime-view.md, and walk through the steps: the model requests a tool call, FunctionInvokingChatClient runs it through ToolCallGuards.InvokeAsync, which logs the call, runs it, and checks the result. Results over 50,000 characters get summarised by a separate model call with no tools, calls that were cut off don't run, and an exception message goes back to the model. The result is then added and the model continues, for up to 10 rounds.

I'll pull the round limit and the tool-choice behaviour on the last round from the GOAL doc and the page, and I'm keeping the answer short. Calling FindPlace for the tool loop would add latency, so I'll skip it and offer the choices instead.

The engine runs each tool call inside a loop, and every call passes through the guards before it runs. The model asks for a tool, the engine runs it, and the result goes back to the model. This repeats until the model answers in text.

For each call, the engine:

1. Logs the call.
2. Runs the tool, with its arguments as data.
3. Checks the result. A result over 50,000 characters is summarised by a separate model call that has no tools. If that fails, the result is cut short.
4. Sends the result back to the model, which continues.

Two cases never run the tool. A call cut off by the output limit has incomplete arguments, so the engine skips it and asks the model to write large content in chunks. A tool that throws sends its exception message back to the model, so the model can correct itself.

The loop allows up to 10 tool rounds per message. On the last round, the tools stay on the request, but the model is told not to use them, so it answers in text.

Source: `src/docs/architecture/06-runtime-view.md`

Tool rounds are capped at 10 per message. The round limit and the last-round rule are also stated in `src/docs/GOAL.md`.
